title: Landing zone concept (multi-account foundation)
hook: A landing zone is a pre-configured multi-account AWS environment with security, networking, and governance baselines. New workloads deploy into accounts carved from this foundation instead of ad-hoc single accounts.

blocks.text: Landing zones provide organization structure (management, security, shared services, workload accounts), baseline networking (hub VPC, IPAM), identity federation, logging aggregation, and guardrails (Service Control Policies). AWS Control Tower automates landing zone setup; custom landing zones use Organizations + CloudFormation StackSets.

entries.plainDefinition: Container for accounts in AWS Organizations

blocks.text: Enterprise migrations fail without account strategy. Interviewers ask how you onboard a new team without compromising security. Landing zones are the answer — repeatable, governed account factory.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: multi-account OU structure, baseline guardrails, shared services, account vending — not one giant account.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Apply baseline guardrails
items.body: SCPs, Config rules, mandatory tags via Control Tower or custom.

items.title: Deploy shared networking
items.body: Hub VPC, Transit Gateway, IPAM pool for spoke CIDR allocation.

items.title: Vend workload accounts
items.body: Account Factory creates account with baseline stacks applied automatically.

snippet.label: StackSet baseline logging
snippet.code:
LogArchiveStackSet:
  Type: AWS::CloudFormation::StackSet
  Properties:
    StackSetName: org-cloudtrail
    PermissionModel: SERVICE_MANAGED
    AutoDeployment:
      Enabled: true
      RetainStacksOnAccountRemoval: false

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Running production workloads in management account. No OU separation for sandbox vs prod. Skipping centralized logging account.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: every new account enrolled in Control Tower within 24h; SCP coverage on all OUs; zero workloads in management account audit.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Single account for everything "because it is simpler" — rejected at enterprise scale. Strong answer: OU structure, guardrails, shared services, account vending.

interviewTakeaways: Landing zone = governed multi-account foundation with baselines.
Management account for billing/governance only — not workloads.
Control Tower or custom StackSets automate repeatable setup.
60s: OUs for Security/Infrastructure/Workloads. SCP guardrails. Hub networking. Account Factory vends governed accounts. Not one shared prod account.
Follow-up: how does landing zone relate to Well-Architected Security pillar?
commonPitfalls: Prod in management account — major governance fail.
Strong answer: OU hierarchy, SCPs, centralized logging, account vending.
No sandbox OU — developers experiment in prod account.
Skipping IPAM — CIDR collisions across spokes.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Landing zone multi-account mirrors multi-repo team boundaries — isolation by default.
npm workspaces separate packages like OUs separate accounts.
